changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 2 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/8632-malformed-picklist-option-loud.md`

- names `packages/i18n/README.md` → `packages/i18n/README.md` — edited by this change

  > Two new strings land in the designer's own `en` / `zh` tables — the metadata-admin console owns its strings in `views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts` and is deliberately outside the ten locale packs (`packages/i18n/README.md`, "Scope — the `engine.*` carve-out").

### `.changeset/9615-locale-count-ten.md`

- names `packages/i18n/README.md` → `packages/i18n/README.md` — edited by this change

  > Correcting the numeral to ten was weighed and refused. A restated count is the construct that permitted the error, and this repository has now watched it recur three times over the same fact — objectui#3351 in a changeset file, objectui#7989 in `packages/i18n/README.md`, and this one in published source. So the number is **gone** rather than corrected: the sentence now claims only what it needs (the key is translated in every locale the package ships) and names `all-locales-key-parity.test.ts` as the instrument that re-derives it. That test asserts the stronger invariant — every pack defines every `en` key — over whatever the pack set is on the day it runs, so an eleventh pack makes the sentence more true rather than false, and there is no figure left to rot (AGENTS.md commandment #9).

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `5638529e6` (merge-base with origin/main): 6 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1913 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2528 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36837476476)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c2f59cf4adee420e043ea4d27923b7fd1a0f1317`
Local-runs: none

Reviewed 2026-10-01T08:54Z from: card #11326 (body and all four comments), PR #11367 (body, file list, and the net diff against `main` — merge-base `2c274e3a8`; `main` has since moved six commits to `5638529e6`, none touching `packages/i18n`, the 7479 changeset or `troubleshooting.md`), and the check-runs on the head, read last. Not read: the dispatch order. Read as claims, not conclusions: `os-dev-report` `5927863627`, ACCEPT `5927897751`, the PR body. Governing texts: objectui `AGENTS.md` at `origin/main`, triage's direction `5925746061`, and objectstack#5419's final ruling as claim `5255335825` quotes it.

### ① Derived judgments

**The widening — three entry exports** (`packages/i18n/src/index.ts` re-exports all three from `./locales/registry.js`). New accept set for each: a tag whose exact form, or whose `split('-')[0]` base, is one of the ten catalogue codes; everything else refused.

- `isBuiltInLanguage` — **right.** Docblock ("exactly, or through its base language") matches the body, `resolveBuiltInLanguage(lang) !== null`. `xx-YY`, `tlh` and `en_US` (underscore, so no split) stay `false`; pinned in `region-locale-fallback-11326.test.tsx` and the seed suite's "ignores a malformed tenant locale".
- `loadBuiltInLocale` — **right.** Resolves the base catalogue and fetches/memoises under the CATALOGUE code (`loaded[code]`, `inFlight` keyed by `code`), so `getLoadedBuiltInLocales()` stays keyed `zh` — which is how `createI18n`, app-shell's `LoadingScreen` (`getLoadedBuiltInLocales()[base]`) and `outboundAgentText` read it. Pinned ("memoises under the catalogue code — `zh-CN` and `zh` share one catalogue"). The docblock's null list drops "a region subtag" — correct.
- `isBuiltInLocaleLoaded` — **right** as the third reader. Left exact it would answer `false` for `zh-CN` while `loadBuiltInLocale('zh-CN')` resolves with no fetch, contradicting its own "no fetch needed". Zero callers outside the registry at head (grep). Named in the PR ("three exported functions … not two") and in the changeset.
- Exact over base: `LAZY_LOCALE_LOADERS` holds `zh ja ko de fr es pt ru ar`, `en` resident — no full-tag key exists, as the PR states. The order is pinned on the normaliser (`pt-BR` wins over `pt`, `pt-PT` falls to `pt`, `xx-YY` null) and on each of the ten resolving to itself. **Right.**
- A narrowing the PR does not state, judged acceptable: a catalogue made resident through `registerBuiltInLocale` under a code OUTSIDE the ten was found by `loadBuiltInLocale`/`isBuiltInLocaleLoaded` at base and is not at head (`hasBuiltInCatalogue` consults `DEFAULT_BUILT_IN_LANGUAGE` and the loaders, not `loaded`). No producer exists: `registerBuiltInLocales()` registers exactly the ten, and `registerBuiltInLocale` is off the entry by its own docblock. Residual, not blocking.

**The language preserved — judged from the pins.** "keeps the user's tag" and "switching to `zh-CN` at runtime" assert `language`, the document `lang` attribute and `localStorage['objectui-locale']` all `zh-CN` while `common.save` renders `保存`. `createI18n` passes `lng` only (no `supportedLngs`, `load` or `lowerCaseLng`), so i18next keeps `zh-CN` as the language and reads the `zh` bundle through its own hierarchy. **Right.**

**`provider.tsx` — three hunks, no call-site fallback.** Verified by line at base `2c274e3a8` and at head: `preloadBootstrapLocale`'s `loadBuiltInLocale(resolveBootstrapLanguage(options))`, the mount effect's `isBuiltInLanguage(currentLang)` guard and its `loadBuiltInLocale(currentLang)`, and `changeLanguage`'s `loadBuiltInLocale(lang)` each appear once at both refs. The inline `seed.split('-')[0]` is gone; `resolveSeedLanguage` is now one `matchLanguageTag(seed, …)` call whose predicate is `canResolveLanguage(code, config)` and nothing else. Docblock point 1 is rewritten because "normalised away" would now be false. **Right**, and it is the reuse triage's direction `5925746061` named.

**Derived effects through `canResolveLanguage` (private), each a consequence of the widening:**
- A stored region tag survives the bootstrap purge on a host with no `loadLanguage` — at base `canResolveLanguage('zh-CN', config, false)` was false and `clearStoredLanguage()` ran; at head it is true. Pinned ("a host with no loader"); the changeset states it. **Right.**
- On a host with a loader, that stored tag is now `provisional: null` (statically known), so the app-locale-list self-heal no longer adjudicates it. **Right**: the value is renderable from the built-in pack, which is what the purge rule protects.
- `offerableLanguages` keeps a region-tagged app locale whose base is built-in even without `loadLanguage`. Unstated; **right** — `canResolveLanguage` is the one judge, by ruling.
- `pickInitialLanguage` is unchanged in effect: it already strips the browser tag to its base before asking.
- The seed tier boots in the stated tag (`zh-CN`, `ja-JP`) — judged in ③.

**The seed rows.** Seven assertions in six rows of `provider-tenant-locale-seed.test.tsx` move `'zh'` to `TENANT_LOCALE` (`'zh-CN'`) and one `'ja'` to `'ja-JP'`. Every row still asserts a specific language; rows 1 and 2 also assert `保存`, and row 2 GAINED that string assertion. **Updated, not weakened.** (Rows 1 and 2 now pin the same pair — a redundancy, not a weakening.)

**The mount effect's side-effect, stated by the PR:** for a stored region tag it adds a `zh-CN` bundle beside the resident `zh` (one extra `added` re-render at mount). Functionally harmless; fixing it is a call-site change the direction excluded. Carried in the PR's notes; not blocking.

**One over-broad sentence, not blocking:** `matchLanguageTag`'s docblock, `resolveSeedLanguage`'s point 1 and the PR body call it "the ONE implementation of this order in the package". `pickLocalized`/`setLocalized` still resolve exact then base (then regional sibling …) over inline locale maps — four `split('-')[0]` sites at head — as the old provider docblock itself cited. They are value resolvers pinned limb-for-limb to a backend twin and rightly untouched; the sentence should say "for a tag to a catalogue or a seed", not "in the package". A wording follow-up.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/11326-i18n-region-locale-fallback.md` — `'@object-ui/i18n': minor`. **Right.** The diff's only published source is `packages/i18n/src/**` (tests aside); the change is an additive accept-set widening of three entry exports; `major` is barred by the version-alignment rule (AGENTS.md 版本号策略, `check-changeset-no-major`). No other package's `src` or contract field moved, so one changeset is the right count. Every sentence checked against the head: the memoisation key, `isBuiltInLocaleLoaded('zh-CN')` answering for `zh`, `xx-YY`/`tlh` refused, "a catalogue keyed by a full tag would win — none ships today", the stored tag kept as written, the no-loader purge that no longer runs, `preloadBootstrapLocale` and `changeLanguage` fetching `zh`, the seed booting in `zh-CN` — all true. ("the tag the signed-in user's `sys_user.locale` applies a moment later" describes the Console's `useSignedInUserLocale`; the seed exists for that host, so it stands.)
- `.changeset/7479-lazy-locale-catalogues.md` — the base blob (4,501 bytes, `origin/main`) is a byte-identical prefix of the head blob (5,072; `cmp -n 4501` exit 0); frontmatter bytes identical; 9 lines appended, 0 removed. The note is dated, cites the card, and describes the base text accurately (the `loadBuiltInLocale` bullet's "`null` for a code this package does not ship"; `isBuiltInLanguage(code)` paired with the ten). Bump levels unchanged. **Right.**
- `Clause-②: yes` — **right**: three published functions widen their accept set. The line itself is bare; the PR's "What this changes" names `isBuiltInLanguage`, `loadBuiltInLocale` and `isBuiltInLocaleLoaded` and deviation 1 says "three exported functions … not two"; the changeset names the same three. The claim's `Why yes` named two; the PR supersedes it with three, declared as a deviation.
- Docs: `packages/i18n/README.md`'s persistence paragraph and built-in-locales block state the rule and the `zh-CN` example (the snippet already imported `isBuiltInLanguage`; `isBuiltInLocaleLoaded` is prose and is exported). `content/docs/guide/troubleshooting.md` §8 step 3 is accurate and distinguishes built-in catalogues from the app's own locale files. The gates that judge all of this on the head — Changeset Bump Policy, Changeset Declaration, Changeset Claim Re-read, Changeset Fixed Group Check, README Export Check, Doc Snippet Type Check, Line Citation Gate — are each `success`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`open_questions[0]` — seed tier, A or B.** Answered by the seat (ACCEPT `5927897751`): B. Judged against the governing text, objectstack#5419's final ruling (2026-08-06T04:14Z) as claim `5255335825` quotes it: `canResolveLanguage` is the sole resolvability judge and the seed must reuse it — 「不得再造第二个"这个 locale 我们有没有"的判定」. Keeping `zh` would need exactly that second, exact-only predicate; B needs none and the `resolveSeedLanguage` docblock holds as written. **The answer stands.**
- **Deviation 1 — `isBuiltInLocaleLoaded` third reader.** Accepted by the seat; judged right in ①; named in PR and changeset.
- **Deviation 2 — seed rows.** Judged in ①: updated, not weakened.
- **Deviation 3 — 7479 note.** Judged in ②: append-only, frontmatter intact.
- **Deviation 4 — README and troubleshooting.** Judged in ②.
- **Out-of-scope findings, carrier none (five, in the PR's Acceptance notes).** The duplicate `zh-CN` bundle at mount, the browser tier still base-stripped, `pickRenderableLocale`'s own copy in app-shell, and `LocaleSwitcher`'s exact checkmark are adequately carried as notes. One I escalate to the seat for a card rather than a note: **`isRTL` matches exactly** (`RTL_LANGUAGES.includes(lang)`), so an `ar-XX` tag that this change now boots AND renders in Arabic gets `dir=ltr`. Same family and no producer in the stock showcase, so not blocking here — but after this head "Arabic chrome, left-to-right" is reachable from a configured `supportedLocales`, which it was not before.
- **The wording residual** ("the ONE implementation") — a follow-up edit, not a re-spin.
- **Check-runs on `c2f59cf4a`**, read last — these are the gate verdicts. 43 runs: 40 `success`, 3 `skipped` (dependabot and the two coverage entries), 0 failed, 0 `in_progress`. At first read (2026-10-01T08:50Z) Test shards 1/8, 2/8 and 4/8 were still `in_progress`; polled, all three settled `success` by 2026-10-01T08:52Z. The families the dev left to CI as NOT MEASURED answer here: README Export Check `success`, Doc Snippet Type Check `success`, and the console production builds (Build & E2E, Bundle Analysis) `success`; Lint, Type Check, Test (dist pins) and all eight test shards `success`.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-11326-i18n-region-locale-fallback`

**VERDICT: PASS**
